findings.area: Autoware dependency anchor and patch compilability
findings.finding: The cached-replay repair is anchored to the wrong header. The patched manager includes <autoware_utils/ros/polling_subscriber.hpp>, calls take_data(), and declares an autoware_utils dependency. The certificate instead hashes common/autoware_universe_utils/include/autoware/universe_utils/ros/polling_subscriber.hpp, whose namespace is autoware::universe_utils and whose method is takeData(). The fixed checkout does not contain the actual autoware_utils header or its pinned revision.
evidence: /private/tmp/clock-audit-autoware/common/autoware_universe_utils/include/autoware/universe/utils/ros/polling_subscriber.hpp is not the recorded path; the actual recorded file is under autoware/universe_utils and is not the included dependency
findings.impact: git apply --check cannot establish that polling_policy::Newest exists in the actual dependency, that the template specialization compiles, or that no-new-message returns nullptr. The cached planner replay claim is unproven.

findings.finding: The Autoware package compiles and exports both standard and experimental virtual-traffic-light plugins. The generated patch removes the remote stamp only from src/scene.cpp and changes only src/manager.cpp; src/experimental/scene.cpp still subtracts clock_->now() - rclcpp::Time(state.stamp), and src/experimental/manager.cpp remains on the cached path.
findings.impact: The narrow statement about the selected standard class is supportable; package-wide or selectable-plugin migration is false on the current patch.

findings.finding: The migration harness stores before_expression, after_expression, and receipt_store_expression as strings but never executes or otherwise interprets them. Its Sample, checked_age, decide, and mutant branches are a separate hand-written model. Mutants alter this model, not either generated patch or target source.
findings.impact: PASS:13 and all-mutants-killed demonstrate internal consistency of the model only. They do not validate compilation, control flow, exception behavior, arithmetic, or state updates in Autoware or CARMA.

findings.finding: The v7 JavaScript local-receipt and same-domain source-event branches have no decision-clock generation field. The C++ since_local_receipt function never compares its two Timestamp relock counters. The cross-domain JavaScript and C++ relation checks bind only the source generation; neither certificate binds the target generation or target-time validity. A target relock therefore remains accepted.
findings.impact: The recorded claim that relocked observations fail closed is only true for a source-side mismatch in one branch. Local receipt and target-clock relock guarantees are not implemented.

findings.area: exception safety and atomic state publication
findings.finding: Both generated patches assign the receipt timestamp before assigning the message payload. Copy assignment of ROS messages can allocate and throw. If an engaged payload assignment throws and an outer layer catches the exception, the old or partially updated payload can remain paired with a new receipt timestamp.
findings.impact: The invariant 'receipt belongs to stored message' is not strongly exception-safe; stale data can be made fresh by a failed update.

findings.finding: The v7 generic C++ kernel uses __int128 checked intermediates, but the actual patches directly subtract steady_clock::time_point values before converting the result. The preceding now < receipt guard does not prevent a positive signed-representation overflow.
findings.impact: The model-level overflow claim cannot be transferred to either patch. The UBSan witness is an extreme representational case and may be unreachable during a normal process lifetime, but no production invariant or checked implementation establishes that boundary.

findings.finding: Autoware's max_delay_sec is an external double and is compared without a finite/nonnegative check; NaN makes delay > max_delay_sec false. The JavaScript relation is a caller-created object, and the C++ RelationCertificate constructor is public; domain labels, timescales, validity, generations, and offset bounds have no authenticated issuer or provenance boundary.
findings.impact: Malformed configuration can disable timeout, while an untrusted caller can mint self-consistent relation metadata. Structural validation is not provenance validation.

findings.finding: The migration generator and certificate pin the v6 obligation JSON and scripts/idea-pilots/clock_obligation.hpp, not the requested v7 obligation certificate and clock_obligation_v7.hpp. They also use candidateId cross-domain-freshness-obligation, while this audit was requested for clock-receipt-semantic-migration. All requested local artifacts are currently untracked.
findings.impact: The migration result is not a content-addressed consequence of the audited v7 kernel, and candidate identity is ambiguous. Current hashes bind bytes for this audit but provide no committed or external timestamp.

findings.finding: CARMA records at callback entry, but Autoware records separately inside each module after polling, dispatch, ID scan, and logging. This is local take/store time, not demonstrated middleware arrival time. Newly delivered duplicates refresh receipt in both paths; only cached planner-cycle replay is intended to be suppressed.
findings.impact: Queue residence is excluded and duplicate delivery is not anti-replay. The semantic target must be named local callback/take age, and new-module/cached-state behavior requires integration tests.

findings.area: migration JavaScript evaluator totality and numeric domain
findings.finding: evaluateReceiptFreshness throws on undefined input, malformed integer text, and unsupported comparators. It accepts arbitrarily large individual BigInt timestamps when their difference fits int64, although the harness stores each operand in int64.
findings.impact: This evaluator is not a total fail-closed oracle over external JSON-like inputs and does not share the harness's operand domain.

findings.finding: Neither project build was attempted. The local environment lacks /opt/ros, colcon, the full dependency workspaces, and the actual Autoware autoware_utils dependency source used by the include. No network lookup was performed, and there was no network execution failure; external dependency resolution was deliberately left unperformed when the audit was stopped.
findings.impact: Compilation, ABI, target tests, callback scheduling, plugin selection, and runtime transition behavior remain unverified hard boundaries.

findings.finding: The source-to-target mapping direction is internally consistent: mapped source bounds are stamp plus offset bounds, and age bounds reverse the mapped endpoints. The typed C++ negative case rejects a relation with reversed domain template parameters.
findings.impact: No relation-sign or endpoint-order counterexample was found within the declared source-to-target convention.

rationale.summary: The semantic migration is coherent in a narrow sense and the two selected diffs are textually applicable, but the evidence does not pass as implementation-valid methodology. The decisive blockers are the wrong Autoware dependency anchor, an unpatched compiled plugin sibling, a self-modeling harness, missing target/local epoch checks, non-atomic receipt publication, unchecked production duration arithmetic, and absent builds.
rationale.whyNotPass: Passing local tests reproduce the authored certificates but do not close the counterexamples or compile the upstream changes. Several supported statements must therefore remain narrowed to current bytes, selected expressions, and model behavior.
rationale.whyReviseRatherThanReject: Replacing source-stamp subtraction with a clearly named local callback/take age is a defensible alternative semantic target, and the fixed-source anchors plus patch dry-runs provide a usable base. The identified defects are substantial but technically repairable without abandoning that target.
